item.title: The Tempest
item.description: Get swept away by Shakespeare's fantastical tale of shipwreck, monsters, romance, and revenge. Exiled from their home, the sorcerer Prospero and his daughter Miranda have survived for years on a remote island. When a ship carrying Prospero's enemies sails into his conjured storm, he finally has a chance to take revenge-and maybe, to weave a brighter future for his daughter. Ensnaring everyone in his labyrinth of sorcery and misdirection, Prospero summons all his power to set his world right.

item.title: Joe Hisaishi with the Colorado Symphony
item.description:
Jump to Tickets ?

PRESENTED BY:

Program

DAVID LANG  Mountain
STEVE REICH  Music for Ensemble and Orchestra
JOE HISAISHI  Concerto for Orchestra

Featured Artists

Joe Hisaishi, conductor

Description

Joe Hisaishi is one of the most celebrated composers of our time. He has established himself as a formidable force in contemporary music for his delicately crafted symphonic and solo works, as well as his globally successful film music. His credits include 12 enchanting, animated Studio Ghibli films, including Hayao Miyazaki's Oscar-winning works, as well as being the Composer-in-Association of Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, and the Composer in Residence for the Philadelphia Orchestra. In his Boettcher Concert Hall debut, Hisaishi will conduct a new Concerto for Orchestra that was co-commissioned by the Colorado Symphony.

Written in five movements and running approximately 45 minutes, the Concerto for Orchestra follows a form made iconic by composers such as Béla Bartók, Witold Lutoslawski, and Zoltán Kodály, placing the orchestra itself at the center of expression. Hisaishi notes, “My aim has been to pursue the pure motion of sound,” drawing on his experience conducting works including Bartók’s Concerto for Orchestra and Steve Reich’s The Desert Music. The work’s first and third movements feature driving rhythmic textures, while the inner movements highlight lyrical solo passages for individual instruments. The final movement brings these rhythmic and lyrical elements together.

Join us for HalfNotes, a fun and family-friendly activity prior to the performance.

item.title: The Who’s TOMMY
item.description: In 1969, The Who created a rock opera that changed the course of music history. And now, it's back in a dazzling all-new production that feels more relevant than ever. Myth and spectacle combine in this fresh reinvention that includes the unforgettable anthems "I'm Free," "See Me, Feel Me," "Sensation" and "Pinball Wizard." After witnessing his father shoot his rival, the young Tommy Walker is lost in the universe, endlessly and obsessively staring into the mirror. An innate knack for pinball catapults him from reticent adolescent to celebrity savior. Tony Award-winning composer Pete Townshend and Tony Award-winning original director Des McAnuff find powerful resonance reexamining this classic story for today.

item.title: Catrinas en Mi Ciudad | Tempus Quartet Outdoor Concert
item.description:
Tempus Quartet is a contemporary classical fusion ensemble from Mexico, known for its innovative approach to reinterpreting the classical repertoire through a dynamic integration of cinematic, popular and Latin American influences. The ensemble bridges traditional chamber music with contemporary soundscapes, creating performances that are both technically refined and emotionally accessible to diverse audiences. Their work challenges conventional concert formats by incorporating elements of visual narratives, stage presence, and theatrical sensibility, positioning them at the intersection of classical music and performative art. Through original arrangements and stylistic reinterpretations, Tempus Quartet expands the expressive possibilities of the string quartet format, engaging both traditional classical audiences and new listeners seeking immersive and cross-genre experiences. Their participation in Catrinas en Mi Ciudad outdoor concert significantly enhances the sonic and atmospheric dimension of the production, serving as a central musical force that supports the narrative arc and emotional intensity of the work.

Through this artistic collaboration, the project also establishes a cultural bridge between Mexico and Colorado, creating an opportunity to share Mexican traditions, foster new connections, and introduce Mexican culture to communities who may encounter it for the first time through the arts. Music, voice, movement, and visual expression/storytelling will come together within a unified narrative exploring universal themes such as memory, life, loss, identity, and the celebration of our roots.

This event is part of the Catrinas en Mi Ciudad exhibit. Learn more at: https://www.artscomplex.com/explore-the-complex/arts-complex-art-exhibits/catrinas-en-mi-ciudad/

item.title: FDR's Very Happy Hour
item.description:
Spend a spirited happy hour with America's 32nd president, back from the great beyond to remind the modern world of his legacy. (C-SPAN ranks him one of the top 3 presidents of all time. He'd like you to know that.)

Inspired by Franklin Delano Roosevelt's real-life habit of hosting cocktail hour nearly every day at the White House to connect and unwind during challenging times, FDR's Very Happy Hour is an immersive happy hour experience that mixes humor and history. Alongside cocktails, mocktails, and soft drinks (it is a happy hour, after all), the evening features game-show trivia, cozy activities to get the room talking, a different "changemaker" from the local community at every performance, and the occasional surprise guest. As FDR invites us to ponder life, a complicated legacy, and the pursuit of community, strangers become friends—and perhaps, together, we can find ways to talk with our neighbors again.  

Prioritizing an accessible experience for as many as possible, open captioning, ASL interpretation, and design of the physical space for wheelchair access are part of the show. (Roosevelt was, after all, a wheelchair user.) If you or anyone in your party has specific access needs, email them to fdrassists@highhardheat.com with the date and time of your performance, and we'll be happy to help.

Each performance features a short interview with a unique "changemaker" from the local community. The confirmed Changemakers so far are as follows:

item.title: Disney's Beauty and the Beast
item.description: Be Our Guest at Beauty and the Beast, Disney's first North American touring production of the beloved musical in over 25 years. This enchanting and timeless tale, filled with the romance and grandeur audiences know and love, has been brought to life like never before, with spectacular new sets and dazzling costumes. The show boasts the Oscar®-winning and Tony Award®-nominated score, including the classic songs "Be Our Guest" and "Beauty and the Beast." Reuniting to create this new production are members of the original Tony Award®-winning artistic team, including composer Alan Menken, lyricist Tim Rice, book writer Linda Woolverton, with direction and choreography by Matt West, scenic design by Stanley A. Meyer, costume design by Ann Hould-Ward and lighting design by Natasha Katz. Beauty and the Beast is the beloved musical that will fill your heart with joy and Disney magic.

item.title: Artists in Conversation: Macbeth
item.description:
Go beyond the performance and discover the stories behind Macbeth.

Join Opera Colorado for an engaging evening of conversation as members of the Macbeth creative team and cast share insights into Verdi's gripping masterpiece. Moderated by Ellie Caulkins Artistic Director & CEO Barbara Lynne Jamison, this lively discussion explores the music, characters, creative process, and artistic vision that bring one of opera's most thrilling dramas to life.

Whether you're attending Macbeth for the first time or returning to a favorite work, Artists in Conversation offers a unique opportunity to hear directly from the artists before opening night.

This event is Pay What You Wish, and advance registration is encouraged.

item.title: Kelly Green Trio
item.description: Award-winning Steinway Artist Kelly Green is a New York City based pianist, vocalist, composer, and bandleader of rare elegance. Her diverse repertoire showcases emotionally potent, genre-defying original music seamlessly woven with reimagined works by Duke Ellington, Mulgrew Miller, Blossom Dearie, and many others. Green and her band effortlessly blend modern innovation with the depth of jazz tradition, bringing audiences something as complex as it is accessible. Originally from Orlando, Florida, Green arrived to New York in 2015. Since then she has performed and recorded with luminaries including Christian McBride, Wycliffe Gordon, Rich Perry, Steve Wilson, Scott Robinson, George Coleman, and Billy Hart. Green released her fifth studio album Corner of My Dreams in 2025 and is set to release her sixth album Eat Your Greens on August 28th of this year. She is an international touring artist, having sold out lauded venues including Birdland, Dizzy’s, and Ronnie Scott’s.

item.title: Denver Film Festival49 | Opening Night Presentation: I Play Rocky
item.description:
Introduced by I Play Rocky screenwriter Peter Gamble
Special Presentation

﻿I Play Rocky is an electrifying true story about an unknown actor with an unshakable belief that he wasn’t just meant to write Rocky—he was meant to be Rocky Balboa. Told “no” at every turn, Sylvester Stallone bets everything on himself, holding the line on playing the lead against seemingly impossible odds. The result is the ultimate underdog story behind the ultimate underdog movie.

Tickets are still available for the 9:00PM set here.
Sy Smith has proven throughout her career that an R&B artist can be progressive while remaining firmly rooted in tradition. Foremost a singer with a vocal range spanning five octaves, Smith began an unending succession of background gigs with Whitney Houston in the late '90s, and has since worked closely with Grammy-winning trumpeter Chris Botti and Grammy-nominated group the Foreign

Exchange, among dozens of other artists. After a brief period signed to a major, Smith established an independent label of her own, an outlet for compositionally solid and sonically adventurous albums including The Syberspace Social (2005), Conflict (2008), Fast and Curious (2012), and the entirely self-produced Sometimes a Rose Will Grow in Concrete (2018). She's consequently known for being a leading force in post-millennial indie soul.” - Andy Kellman Sy raises her own bar and then leaps over it with her latest offering “Until We Meet Again” - her critically-acclaimed album produced by Zo! & Tall Black Guy, executive produced by Phonte Coleman and released on +FE Music in January 2024. This mellifluously soulful LP is drawing comparisons to Minnie Riperton and Deniece Williams and is already being called “the album of the year” by a few critics. Music journalist Mark Chappelle says “Smith evokes multiple traditions at once. With the sincerity of Diana Ross dedicating “Missing You” to Marvin Gaye, Smith lets her voice levitate until it breaks—as if just the right frequency could resurrect a loved one.”

item.title: The Firebird with Cleo Parker Robinson Dance & John Williams Horn Concerto
item.description:
Jump to Tickets ?

PRESENTED BY:

Program

ELGAR  Introduction and Allegro, Op. 47
JOHN WILLIAMS  Horn Concerto
STRAVINSKY  The Firebird

Featured Artists

Michael Francis, conductor
Michael Thornton, horn
Cleo Parker Robinson Dance

  

Description

Stravinsky’s The Firebird plunges listeners into a vivid world of Russian folklore, stitching together fairy tales, magic, and danger into one of the most electrifying scores of the 20th century. The ballet’s myth-like storyline features a magical Firebird, who helps a young prince rescue a coterie of princesses from Kashchey, an evil sorcerer. Stravinsky’s brilliant orchestrations paint a colorful musical portrait that will be brought to life onstage alongside Cleo Parker Robinson Dance.

The spotlight turns to the Colorado Symphony’s own Principal Horn Michael Thornton in John Williams’ Horn Concerto. Williams himself described the horn as an instrument that "stirs memories of powerful things, of noble and beautiful things," whose very sound "invites us to dream backward to ancient time." His concerto draws on that deeply evocative timbre, crafting five movements that explore a sweeping range of moods — from the distant bells of "Angelus," through the wild energy of "The Hunt," to the quiet introspection of "Nocturne." In Thornton’s hands, audiences will hear not just technical brilliance but a voice that evokes memory and myth. The program opens with Elgar’s Introduction and Allegro, a delightful showcase for string orchestra that sets the stage for an evening of musical drama led by guest conductor Michael Francis.

Prelude: Join us before the concert to dive deeper into the music, this weekend with Associate Principal Horn Kolio Plachkov at 6:30 PM (FRI & SAT) and 12:00 PM (SUN).

Talkback: After the performance on SAT, OCT 24 join Conductor Michael Francis and Principal Horn Michael Thornton for a peek behind the curtain.
